newsitem.title: GERMANY: Euro share indices by Jan 1998-German bourse.
newsitem.headline: Euro share indices by Jan 1998-German bourse.

text.p: A set of new European share indices being developed by bourses in France, Germany and Switzerland will be up and running by January 31, 1998 at the latest, the German stock exchange said on Tuesday.

The three participating exchanges on Monday signed a declaration of intent to launch the indices, which are designed to meet changing investment needs in the run-up to the launch of Europe's single currency in January 1999, the bourse said in a statement.

"The trend of taking investment decisions less on the basis of country-specific factors and more on the basis of cross-border sector analyses will be strengthened by the introduction of a single European currency," the bourse said.

There will be four products in all. Two indices will cover the leading companies and a broader spectrum of companies respectively in the entire European zone, and a similar pair of indices will be produced for countries in the euro zone.
The German bourse noted that the exchanges in the partnership together represented more than half of the total market capitalisation in Europe.
Last May, the FTSE International and Amsterdam Exchanges signed a co-operation deal covering pan-European indices.

The deal called for FTSE International, best known for managing London's FTSE 100 index, and the London stock Exchange to take over the running of Amsterdam Exchange's Europtop 100 index and introduction of a complementary and wider- based European index.
Both indices are aimed at supporting the growing market in pan-European trading.
